facts.label: Present perfect ou passado simples
facts.sub: Sem hora: have/has + particípio (I have seen it). Com hora: passado simples (I saw it yesterday). Yesterday, last night e on Friday pedem o passado.

facts.label: Sem hora
facts.sub: Use present perfect quando o momento exato não importa: I have seen that film. Fale da experiência ou do resultado. Use have/has + particípio e palavras como ever, never, already, just e yet.

facts.label: Com hora
facts.sub: Use passado simples quando disser quando aconteceu: I saw it yesterday. Palavras como yesterday, last night, on Friday e two days ago pedem o passado simples. Não use have com elas.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Yesterday goes with the simple past.
We say “I have seen it yesterday”.
items.why: We say I saw it yesterday.

items.s: Present perfect talks about experience without a time.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Yesterday goes with the simple past. → Verdadeiro (Yes: I saw it yesterday.)
We say “I have seen it yesterday”. → Falso (We say I saw it yesterday.)
Present perfect talks about experience without a time. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A Sunday in the living room · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cold Sunday morning in Chicago. Gray light comes through the curtain of a small living room. A blanket and two pillows lie on the sofa. Joy looks for her keys under a pile of books. Her roommate Max walks in with sleepy eyes. They start to talk about the last two days.

“Max, have you seen my keys? I had them yesterday.” says Joy. “I haven’t seen them today, but I saw them on the sofa last night.” says Max. “Thanks! I have looked everywhere, but I didn’t check the sofa.” says Joy.
